title: One surface path and one edge loop: SurfaceSpline, SurfaceRing, PlaneSurfaceLoop and RingCandidates compose TracedSurfacePath instead of copying its fields
description:
Repo plan merge 3C.16. TracedSurfacePath (positions, surfacePositions, vertexId, edgeId, faceId, fraction, closed) is the core path; SurfaceSpline (17-102) copies the same arrays and converts both ways (followPath :329, surfacePath :415) between double and float; SurfaceRing and SurfaceSpline both repeat polyline, markedByEdgeId, markedEdgeIds, markedEdgeCount, unresolvedGaps, length, meanRadius, centroid; RingCandidates (39-87) is the same as struct-of-arrays; PlaneSurfaceLoop (28-37) is a subset. Choose float or double once; the ring and spline types hold a TracedSurfacePath plus an edge-loop value (mask, ids, count, gaps) and its measures. Data classes stop running algorithms (SurfaceRing.through/tightenedOrNull :83,107, PlaneSurfaceLoop.walk :69, RingCandidates statics :144,175 move to their tracer/builder). RingTool reads these fields directly, so this lands after the tool merge.

Rulings that apply (user, 2026-10-17): no class renames where avoidable (classes move package and keep their names; Camera stays the parent of Camera2D/Camera3D; MeshNode keeps its name); scenes and tools keep declaring their controls in a method mapping keys to functions; Palettes is the colour class patch colours merge into. Full plan and evidence: $REPO_HOME/ai-workspace/reports/repo-plan-2026-10-17.md.
definition-of-done:
1. No path or ring type duplicates TracedSurfacePath's arrays; no float/double round trip.
2. Ring and bisector fingerprints on the crawfish and fertility DSL copies byte-identical; saved DSLs reload identically.
3. Unit suite passes; launch entry and screenshot of the ring scene.
testing-plan:
1. Fingerprints before and after.
2. mvn test; BisectorTest, ring tests.
changes-made:
MESH-62 implemented (uncommitted, worktree mesh-62). One path type, one edge loop, double precision throughout. TracedSurfacePath (double) is the only path: it gains its measures (length, centroid, meanRadius, set by measure()) and drawnPolyline(xyz), the one-way float conversion for GL overlays and CurveGeometry; polylineLength/packedFloatPositions are gone. The edge-loop value is the existing EdgeMarks class (no new class): an instance holds markedByEdgeId, markedEdgeIds, markedEdgeCount, unresolvedGaps; its bundle statics are unchanged; ConformingLoopSnap.edgeLoop(mesh, path) returns one. SurfaceSpline holds path + marks (dropped polyline, surfacePolyline, pointVertexId/EdgeId/FaceId/Fraction, open, length, meanRadius, centroidX/Y/Z, markedByEdgeId/Ids/Count, unresolvedGaps; deleted followPath, surfacePath (the double->float->double round trip), largestDeviationFrom (no caller)). SurfaceRing holds path, seed, marks, seedMarks (dropped polyline, seedPolyline, seedLength, centroid, meanRadius, closed and the mark fields). RingCandidates holds TracedSurfacePath[] path, EdgeMarks[] marks, double[] seedLength (dropped polylineOffset/polylinePoint/markedEdgeOffset/markedEdgeId/centroid/length/meanRadius, edgeIdsOf, ringPointCount); its statics markedEdgeComponents/marksOneClosedCycle moved to the builder RingCandidateExtractor (marksOneClosedCycle, CYCLE_VERTEX_DEGREE; markedEdgeComponents had only a benchmark caller and is gone). PlaneSurfaceLoop keeps its walk (it is the walker) but its result is a measured TracedSurfacePath (path, null when the walk did not close); its public edgeId/crossingFraction/polyline/stepCount/closed/length and asTracedPath are gone, the walk buffers are private. GirdlingPlane drops its polyline/edgeCount/length aliases of the cut. SplineAnchorFit and AuthoredSplineRing take double references (the fit no longer rounds trace points or geodesic crossings to float). LineSet.pathStep takes double xyz. RingCandidateExtractor keeps accepted SurfaceRings instead of six float candidate arrays.
Bug fixed on the way, with regression test BisectorTest.aGraphRingAuthoredAsEdgesWallsWithItsOwnEdgesNotItsFittedSpline (fails on master: 76 stale ids vs 96): a graph ring adopted from an edge mask kept the fitted spline's markedEdgeIds while its mask was the graph's, so bisector wall snapping used edges the ring does not draw; it now carries the mask's own ids and its path/measures are the loop it follows.
Verification: ring sessions on fertility_rings and crawfish_rings (ui-state edge-mark fingerprints, mesh fingerprint, regions before and after a bisector, three bisects, a confirmed bisector, rings add seed and tightened, connection with and without walls) identical in every fingerprint, edge count, length, region and bisector; the DSL fixtures sweep (all 50 DSLs under resources/dsl, 46 of which load on master too; mesh fingerprints and edge-mark fingerprints) byte-identical; differences only in measures: meanRadius (now the mean over the loop's distinct points; before, a closed loop's first point counted twice; up to 0.5%), minimumInteriorAngleDegrees (~1e-4 degrees, measured on double positions), centroids in the last float digit, connection girths ~1e-9 relative (the plane loop's closing span in double). Quad suite 14/14 MATCH (signatures and screenshots) against /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/mesh-62-before. Unit suite 553/553 (mvn test -pl annotations,ixdar-app). Ring scene screenshot tmp/mesh-62-ring-tool.png (fertility_rings, region colours on) is bit-identical to master's (tmp/mesh-62-ring-tool-master.png, image-diff rmse 0). Launch entry 'MESH-62: ring-tool'. Scripts tmp/m62_regress.py, tmp/m62_compare.py; captures tmp/m62-base, tmp/m62-after (baseline taken from a snapshot of the untouched worktree).
Open: SurfaceRing.through/tightenedOrNull still build rings on the data class: there is no tracer/builder class to receive them without a new class or a geodesic->rings dependency. PlaneSurfaceLoop.walk stays: PlaneSurfaceLoop is the walker, not a data type. SurfaceGeodesics' traced* buffers (the engine's last-trace output) are out of scope.
review-summary: SurfaceSpline, SurfaceRing, RingCandidates and PlaneSurfaceLoop hold one TracedSurfacePath and one EdgeMarks edge loop instead of float copies of the path's arrays and measures. Each type repeated the same fields and converted between double and float, so consumers read different copies of one path.
